name: Take It to the Streets!

pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.label: Pick a grievance
pick.heading: Pick a small annoyance and start a movement
lead: History is full of great causes. This isn’t one of them. Everybody has a small, daily annoyance that makes them quietly furious: the lecture at 8 a.m., the printer that jams before every deadline, the Bürgeramt appointment you can only get in three months’ time in Marzahn.
Choose one and turn it into a campaign: a demand, a slogan and a plan for getting noticed. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The more trivial, the better.*
pick.note: Obviously nobody is actually marching anywhere. Keep it kind: campaign against a thing, not against a group of people.

rows: Which small thing makes you quietly furious?
What exactly should change, and who has to change it?
Short enough for a placard, catchy enough to chant
A march, a petition, a sit-in, a hashtag, something stranger?
Who suffers most from this, and who would you have to win over?
What would make you lose public support?

values.demand: Any appointment, anywhere in Berlin, within two weeks. If the city can’t manage that, the Bürgeramt comes to you, in a van.
values.slogan: “What do we want? An appointment! When do we want it? Some time in the next eleven weeks!”
values.how: A queue-in: five hundred people standing politely in a perfect line round the Rotes Rathaus from 7 a.m., each holding a little paper number. Very German, and very hard to object to.
values.who: Every Erasmus student who has ever tried to register an address, and anyone who has refreshed the booking page at midnight.
values.line: Blocking the trams. Berliners will forgive almost anything, but not making them late.

yours.heading: Your campaign
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your movement in a few sentences.
